```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(cli.progress_show_after = Inf)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Thakre 2026 built two independent population PK models from the same pediatric
DORA study: one for glecaprevir (GLE) and one for pibrentasvir (PIB), the two
components of the fixed-dose combination Mavyret. Each is packaged as its own
model and both are validated here.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Thakre_2026_glecaprevir"))$reference`
* Glecaprevir: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Thakre_2026_glecaprevir"))$description`
* Pibrentasvir: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Thakre_2026_pibrentasvir"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-026-01637-1> (open access, with an
  electronic supplementary document holding the demographics, Table S1)

# Population

The analysis pooled 126 patients aged 3 to 17 years with chronic hepatitis C
from the phase 2/3 DORA study (NCT03067129). Part 1 (cohort 1, n = 47) enrolled
adolescents aged 12 to <18 years who took the adult tablets (GLE/PIB
300 mg/120 mg once daily). Part 2 enrolled children aged 9 to <12 (cohort 2),
6 to <9 (cohort 3) and 3 to <6 years (cohort 4); 79 of them were analysed. The
children took a pediatric coated-granule formulation dosed by weight band, first
at a GLE/PIB dose ratio of 40/15 mg and then at the final 50/20 mg ratio
(150/60 mg for 12 to <20 kg, 200/80 mg for 20 to <30 kg, 250/100 mg for 30 to
<45 kg; Table 1). Body weight ranged 12.7-108.9 kg (median 36.45 kg), 55.6% of
patients were female, 70.6% White, 15.9% Asian and 5.6% Black. None had
cirrhosis; genotypes 1-4 were represented (ESM Table S1). The models were fitted
to 693 GLE and 693 PIB plasma concentrations with NONMEM 7.4.3 (FOCE-INT).

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Thakre_2026_glecaprevir")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. The table
collects them.

| Equation / parameter | GLE value | PIB value | Source location |
|----------------------|-----------|-----------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL/F at 70 kg, L/day) | log(1830) | log(2170) | Table 2 / Table 3 |
| `lvc` (V2/F at 70 kg, L) | log(358) | log(528) | Table 2 / Table 3 |
| `lq` (Q/F, L/day) | -- | log(765) | Table 3 |
| `lvp` (V3/F, L) | -- | log(3750) | Table 3 |
| `ltlag` (ALAG1, day) | -- | log(0.0556) | Table 3 |
| `lkaratio` (absorption factor) | log(3.65) | log(2.47) | Tables 2 and 3, footnote b |
| `e_wt_cl` (weight on CL/F) | 1.04 | 0.440 | Tables 2 and 3 |
| `e_wt_vc` (weight on V2/F) | 1.19 | 0.757 | Tables 2 and 3 |
| `e_form_granule_fdepot` (F1, Part 2) | 0.800 FIX | 1.20 FIX | Tables 2 and 3; Methods, Model Development |
| `etalcl` (variance) | 1.39 | 0.359 | Tables 2 and 3, IIV |
| `etalvc` (variance) | 1.52 | 0.170 | Tables 2 and 3, IIV |
| `propSd` | sqrt(0.568) = 0.7537 | sqrt(0.229) = 0.4785 | Tables 2 and 3, sigma^2 (proportional) |
| `cl = exp(lcl + etalcl) * (WT/70)^e_wt_cl` | | | ESM Fig. S3 / S4 legends; Methods (70 kg reference) |
| `ka = karatio * cl / vc` | | | Tables 2 and 3 footnote b; Results, Model Results |
| `f(depot) = 1 + (e_form_granule_fdepot - 1) * FORM_GRANULE` | | | Methods, Model Development |
| One-compartment (GLE) / two-compartment with lag (PIB) | | | Results, Model Results |

The tables also print the derived typical absorption rate constants, 18.6 1/day
(GLE) and 10.1 1/day (PIB). They follow from the absorption factor, CL/F and
V2/F, and the check below confirms the transcription:

```{r derived-ka}
ka_check <- tibble::tibble(
  drug = c("glecaprevir", "pibrentasvir"),
  ka_model = c(3.65 * 1830 / 358, 2.47 * 2170 / 528),
  ka_paper = c(18.6, 10.1)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (ka_model / ka_paper - 1))
knitr::kable(ka_check, digits = 2, caption = "Derived typical ka (1/day) at 70 kg.")
# Rounding of the printed table values only; a mis-transcribed CL, V or factor
# moves this by far more than 1%.
stopifnot(all(abs(ka_check$pct_diff) < 1))
```

# Virtual cohorts

Two designs from the paper are reproduced, both at steady state after 14 daily
doses with rich sampling over the last dosing interval (day 13 to day 14):

1. **DORA cohorts (Table 4 and Figure 3).** Cohort 1 adolescents on the adult
   tablet (300/120 mg) and cohorts 2-4 children on the pediatric granules at the
   final 50/20 mg dose ratio. Body weights are drawn from a normal distribution
   with each cohort's mean and SD, truncated to its observed range (ESM
   Table S1). 100 virtual patients per cohort.
2. **Virtual children (Results, "Simulated GLE and PIB Steady-State
   Exposures").** The paper drew 10,000 children with weight uniform on
   12-45 kg and dosed them by weight band. Here 200 per band are drawn from the
   same uniform distribution within each band.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20260526)

# Truncated-normal draw by rejection, used for the DORA cohort weights.
rtruncnorm_wt <- function(n, mean, sd, lower, upper) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- rnorm(2 * n, mean, sd)
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lower & x <= upper])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

design <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,                            ~design,     ~n,  ~gle, ~pib, ~granule, ~wt_mean, ~wt_sd, ~wt_lo, ~wt_hi,
  "Cohort 1 (12 to <18 y, tablet)",  "DORA",      100, 300,  120,  0L,       59.22,    14.08,  32.0,   108.9,
  "Cohort 2 (9 to <12 y)",           "DORA",      100, 250,  100,  1L,       36.92,    4.44,   29.4,   44.3,
  "Cohort 3 (6 to <9 y)",            "DORA",      100, 200,  80,   1L,       24.45,    3.50,   19.6,   33.5,
  "Cohort 4 (3 to <6 y)",            "DORA",      100, 150,  60,   1L,       15.86,    2.01,   12.7,   21.2,
  "12 to <20 kg",                    "Virtual",   200, 150,  60,   1L,       NA,       NA,     12,     20,
  "20 to <30 kg",                    "Virtual",   200, 200,  80,   1L,       NA,       NA,     20,     30,
  "30 to <45 kg",                    "Virtual",   200, 250,  100,  1L,       NA,       NA,     30,     45
)
design$id_offset <- c(0L, cumsum(design$n)[-nrow(design)])

subjects <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(design)), function(i) {
  d <- design[i, ]
  wt <- if (d$design == "DORA") {
    rtruncnorm_wt(d$n, d$wt_mean, d$wt_sd, d$wt_lo, d$wt_hi)
  } else {
    runif(d$n, d$wt_lo, d$wt_hi)
  }
  tibble::tibble(
    id = d$id_offset + seq_len(d$n),
    group = d$group,
    design = d$design,
    WT = wt,
    FORM_GRANULE = d$granule,
    amt_gle = d$gle,
    amt_pib = d$pib
  )
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(subjects$id))

dose_days <- 0:13
obs_days <- 13 + seq(0, 24, by = 0.5) / 24

events_base <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  subjects |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = dose_days) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  subjects |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_days) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt_gle = 0, amt_pib = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

events_gle <- events_base |> dplyr::mutate(amt = amt_gle)
events_pib <- events_base |> dplyr::mutate(amt = amt_pib)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod_gle <- readModelDb("Thakre_2026_glecaprevir")
mod_pib <- readModelDb("Thakre_2026_pibrentasvir")

keep_cols <- c("group", "design")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260526)
sim_gle <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_gle, events = events_gle, keep = keep_cols) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(drug = "Glecaprevir")
sim_pib <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pib, events = events_pib, keep = keep_cols) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(drug = "Pibrentasvir")

# The population solves keep their between-subject variability.
iiv_check <- dplyr::bind_rows(sim_gle, sim_pib) |>
  dplyr::distinct(drug, id, cl, WT) |>
  dplyr::group_by(drug) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sd_eta_cl = sd(log(cl) - ifelse(drug == "Glecaprevir", 1.04, 0.44) * log(WT / 70)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# Expected sqrt(1.39) = 1.18 (GLE) and sqrt(0.359) = 0.60 (PIB).
stopifnot(all(iiv_check$sd_eta_cl > 0.4))

sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(sim_gle, sim_pib) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, group, design, drug) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time_h = 24 * time, tad_h = time_h - 13 * 24)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(sim$Cc)))
```

A handful of glecaprevir patients draw an extreme V2/F (the paper's IIV variance
is 1.52, about 189% CV) and so an elimination half-life of minutes; their
profiles fall between the 0.5 h output times and their solved concentrations
sit at the integrator's absolute tolerance, a little above or below zero. The
undershoot is asserted to be noise and floored at zero.

```{r floor}
# Measured undershoot about -3e-7 ng/mL against a cohort maximum above 1e4.
stopifnot(all(sim$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim$Cc)))
sim <- dplyr::mutate(sim, Cc = pmax(Cc, 0))
```

## Steady-state profiles (Figure 2 analogue)

Figure 2 of the paper is a prediction-corrected VPC of concentration versus time
since the last dose. Without the observed data the prediction correction cannot
be reproduced, so the figure below shows the simulated 5th, 50th and 95th
percentiles over the steady-state dosing interval in each DORA cohort.
Percentiles below the assay's lower limit of quantification (about 1 ng/mL for
both analytes) are drawn at that limit (dotted line).

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(design == "DORA") |>
  dplyr::group_by(drug, group, tad_h) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    Q50 = quantile(Cc, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(Q05, Q50, Q95), function(x) pmax(x, 1))) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad_h, Q50, colour = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~drug, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time since last dose (h)",
    y = "Plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Simulated median and 90% interval at steady state; compare Figure 2 of Thakre 2026."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```

# PKNCA validation

AUC24 is computed with PKNCA over the last dosing interval (hours 312-336),
grouped by drug and simulation group, with the linear trapezoidal rule the paper
used for its own simulations.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time_h, Cc, drug, group)

dose_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  events_gle |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |> dplyr::mutate(drug = "Glecaprevir"),
  events_pib |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |> dplyr::mutate(drug = "Pibrentasvir")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time_h = 24 * time) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time_h, amt, drug, group)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time_h | drug + group + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time_h | drug + group + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 312, end = 336, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  conc_obj, dose_obj,
  intervals = intervals,
  options = list(auc.method = "linear")
))

auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::select(id, drug, group, auc24 = PPORRES)
stopifnot(nrow(auc) == 2 * nrow(subjects), all(is.finite(auc$auc24)))
```

## Comparison against the published steady-state AUC24

The paper reports two sets of geometric mean AUC24 values (ng*h/mL):

- **Virtual children by weight band** (Results, "Simulated GLE and PIB
  Steady-State Exposures"): a population simulation from the final models, the
  same kind of calculation as this vignette. This is the validation target.
- **DORA cohorts** (Table 4): geometric means of the *post hoc* individual
  estimates of the patients who received the final dose. These reflect the
  observed patients' empirical Bayes estimates, not the population
  distribution: in children they lie 30-40% above what the typical-value model
  predicts for their weights. For the cohort 1 adolescents the two agree
  (typical-value prediction at the median 57.7 kg about 4800 ng*h/mL for
  glecaprevir and 1440 ng*h/mL for pibrentasvir, against 5020 and 1590). A population
  simulation is not expected to reproduce them and they are shown for context
  only.

For a log-normal AUC24 the geometric mean equals the median, so the simulated
medians (the summary `ncaComparisonTable()` uses) are compared with the
published geometric means. The median is also robust to the few glecaprevir
tail patients whose grid trapezoid AUC is near zero.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug,          ~group,                           ~auclast,
  "Glecaprevir",  "12 to <20 kg",                   6340,
  "Glecaprevir",  "20 to <30 kg",                   6020,
  "Glecaprevir",  "30 to <45 kg",                   4600,
  "Glecaprevir",  "Cohort 1 (12 to <18 y, tablet)", 5020,
  "Glecaprevir",  "Cohort 2 (9 to <12 y)",          7100,
  "Glecaprevir",  "Cohort 3 (6 to <9 y)",           6960,
  "Glecaprevir",  "Cohort 4 (3 to <6 y)",           8490,
  "Pibrentasvir", "12 to <20 kg",                   1410,
  "Pibrentasvir", "20 to <30 kg",                   1700,
  "Pibrentasvir", "30 to <45 kg",                   1720,
  "Pibrentasvir", "Cohort 1 (12 to <18 y, tablet)", 1590,
  "Pibrentasvir", "Cohort 2 (9 to <12 y)",          2060,
  "Pibrentasvir", "Cohort 3 (6 to <9 y)",           1900,
  "Pibrentasvir", "Cohort 4 (3 to <6 y)",           1820
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = dplyr::filter(as.data.frame(nca_res), PPTESTCD == "auclast"),
  reference = published,
  by = c("drug", "group"),
  units = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Steady-state AUC24: published geometric means (weight bands from the",
    "Results; DORA cohorts from Table 4, post hoc) vs. simulated medians.",
    "* differs from the published value by more than 20%."
  )
)
```

The glecaprevir rows carry large Monte-Carlo error: the CL/F IIV variance of
1.39 gives a 200-patient median a standard error of about
1.25 x sqrt(1.39 / 200) = 10%, and a 100-patient median about 15%, so single
rows (here the 30 to <45 kg band and cohort 1) can miss by 20-45% with a correct
model. The glecaprevir rows for the cohort 2-4 children are further starred for
the reason given above: Table 4 summarises post hoc estimates of the observed
children, whose exposures were higher than the population model predicts. The
gate below therefore pools the 600 virtual children per drug, and the seed-free
check after it removes the Monte-Carlo error entirely.

```{r nca-gate}
virtual <- published |>
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("^Cohort", group)) |>
  dplyr::rename(pub = auclast)
gate <- auc |>
  dplyr::inner_join(virtual, by = c("drug", "group")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(drug) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), median_ratio = median(auc24 / pub), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(gate, digits = 3, caption = "Virtual children: median of simulated AUC24 / published geometric mean, pooled over the three weight bands.")
# Pooled over 600 patients per drug the glecaprevir median carries a
# Monte-Carlo SE of about 6% and pibrentasvir about 3%; measured 1.16 (GLE)
# and 0.97 (PIB). A mis-transcribed CL/F, F1 ratio or unit moves the ratio far
# outside this band.
stopifnot(nrow(gate) == 2, all(gate$n == 600), all(abs(gate$median_ratio - 1) < 0.3))
```

### Seed-free check of the virtual-children geometric means

With exact steady-state AUC24 = F x Dose / CL and log-normal CL/F, the expected
geometric mean over a weight band is F x Dose / CL evaluated at the band's
geometric-mean weight; the random effects drop out. For weight uniform on
[a, b] the geometric-mean weight is exp((b ln b - b - a ln a + a) / (b - a)).

```{r closed-form-gm}
band <- tibble::tibble(
  group = c("12 to <20 kg", "20 to <30 kg", "30 to <45 kg"),
  a = c(12, 20, 30), b = c(20, 30, 45),
  gle = c(150, 200, 250), pib = c(60, 80, 100)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(wt_gm = exp((b * log(b) - b - a * log(a) + a) / (b - a)))
expected_gm <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  band |> dplyr::mutate(drug = "Glecaprevir", gm = 0.8 * gle / (1830 * (wt_gm / 70)^1.04) * 24000),
  band |> dplyr::mutate(drug = "Pibrentasvir", gm = 1.2 * pib / (2170 * (wt_gm / 70)^0.44) * 24000)
) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(virtual, by = c("drug", "group")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (gm / pub - 1)) |>
  dplyr::select(drug, group, wt_gm, gm, pub, pct_diff)
expected_gm |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Drug" = drug, "Weight band" = group, "Geometric-mean weight (kg)" = wt_gm,
    "Expected GM AUC24" = gm, "Published GM AUC24" = pub, "% diff" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
# Deterministic: measured +2% to +16% (GLE) and -1% to +9% (PIB). Part of the
# gap is that the paper integrated its simulated day-14 profiles over the
# intensive-PK sampling times only, and that pibrentasvir is 3-8% short of steady
# state on day 14 (next section).
stopifnot(all(abs(expected_gm$pct_diff) < 20))
```

## Deterministic steady-state check

At steady state the dosing-interval AUC equals F x Dose / CL for both models
(linear elimination from the central compartment). A typical-value solve
reproduces that closed form, confirming the formulation factor, weight scaling
and unit conversion together. Pibrentasvir's slow peripheral phase
(Q/V3 = 0.2 1/day) is still accumulating on day 14, so this check doses for
60 days; the day-14 AUC24 of the paper's design is shown alongside.

```{r closed-form}
typ <- subjects |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::slice(1) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  typ |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = 0:59) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  typ |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = c(13 + seq(0, 24, by = 0.5) / 24, 59 + seq(0, 24, by = 0.5) / 24)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt_gle = 0, amt_pib = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

# omega = NA removes the random effects for this solve only. rxode2 warns on
# every multi-subject solve without omega; that one warning is expected here.
solve_typical <- function(mod, events) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, omega = NA, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  ) |>
    as.data.frame()
}
sim_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  solve_typical(mod_gle, dplyr::mutate(ev_typ, amt = amt_gle)) |> dplyr::mutate(drug = "Glecaprevir"),
  solve_typical(mod_pib, dplyr::mutate(ev_typ, amt = amt_pib)) |> dplyr::mutate(drug = "Pibrentasvir")
)

trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
closed <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(drug, id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    auc_day14 = trap(24 * time[time <= 14], Cc[time <= 14]),
    auc_day60 = trap(24 * time[time >= 59], Cc[time >= 59]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(subjects, id, WT, FORM_GRANULE, amt_gle, amt_pib), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cl70 = ifelse(drug == "Glecaprevir", 1830, 2170),
    ewt = ifelse(drug == "Glecaprevir", 1.04, 0.44),
    frel = ifelse(FORM_GRANULE == 1, ifelse(drug == "Glecaprevir", 0.8, 1.2), 1),
    dose = ifelse(drug == "Glecaprevir", amt_gle, amt_pib),
    auc_closed = frel * dose / (cl70 * (WT / 70)^ewt) * 24 * 1000,
    pct_diff_day60 = 100 * (auc_day60 / auc_closed - 1),
    pct_diff_day14 = 100 * (auc_day14 / auc_closed - 1)
  )
closed |>
  dplyr::select(drug, WT, FORM_GRANULE, dose, auc_closed, auc_day60, pct_diff_day60, auc_day14, pct_diff_day14) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Drug" = drug, "Weight (kg)" = WT, "Granules" = FORM_GRANULE, "Dose (mg)" = dose,
    "F x Dose / CL" = auc_closed, "AUC24 day 60" = auc_day60, "% diff day 60" = pct_diff_day60,
    "AUC24 day 14" = auc_day14, "% diff day 14" = pct_diff_day14
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical-value AUC24 (ng*h/mL), 0.5 h trapezoid vs. the steady-state closed form.")
# Same parameters on both sides: at day 60 the gap is trapezoid error over the
# 0.5 h grid only.
stopifnot(all(abs(closed$pct_diff_day60) < 2))
```

## Exposure distributions (Figure 3)

Figure 3 compares the per-patient AUC24 distributions with the adult target
ranges (GLE 2400-9600 ng*h/mL, PIB 715-2860 ng*h/mL; two-fold around the adult
geometric means).

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
targets <- tibble::tibble(
  drug = rep(c("Glecaprevir", "Pibrentasvir"), each = 2),
  bound = c(2400, 9600, 715, 2860)
)
auc |>
  dplyr::filter(group %in% design$group[design$design == "DORA"]) |>
  # The few glecaprevir tail patients whose profile falls between output times
  # have a grid AUC near zero; they are drawn at the 100 ng*h/mL axis floor.
  dplyr::mutate(auc24 = pmax(auc24, 100)) |>
  ggplot(aes(group, auc24)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(data = targets, aes(yintercept = bound), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~drug, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Steady-state AUC24 (ng*h/mL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Simulated DORA cohorts; dashed lines are the adult target ranges (Figure 3 of Thakre 2026).",
      "Values below 100 are drawn at 100.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

The simulated spread is reported as the geometric %CV next to the paper's
Table 4 values. The paper's values come from post hoc estimates in 17-44
patients per cohort and the simulation draws from the full IIV, so only the
order of magnitude is compared.

```{r cv-table}
auc |>
  dplyr::filter(group %in% design$group[design$design == "DORA"]) |>
  dplyr::group_by(drug, group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sim_gcv_pct = 100 * sqrt(exp(var(log(auc24))) - 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tibble::tribble(
      ~drug,          ~group,                           ~paper_gcv_pct,
      "Glecaprevir",  "Cohort 1 (12 to <18 y, tablet)", 184,
      "Glecaprevir",  "Cohort 2 (9 to <12 y)",          140,
      "Glecaprevir",  "Cohort 3 (6 to <9 y)",           133,
      "Glecaprevir",  "Cohort 4 (3 to <6 y)",           175,
      "Pibrentasvir", "Cohort 1 (12 to <18 y, tablet)", 56,
      "Pibrentasvir", "Cohort 2 (9 to <12 y)",          71,
      "Pibrentasvir", "Cohort 3 (6 to <9 y)",           57,
      "Pibrentasvir", "Cohort 4 (3 to <6 y)",           66
    ),
    by = c("drug", "group")
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Drug" = drug, "Cohort" = group,
    "Simulated geometric %CV" = sim_gcv_pct,
    "Thakre 2026 Table 4 %CV" = paper_gcv_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **CL/F-V2/F covariance not reported.** The paper states that correlated random
  effects were included for CL/F and V2/F, but Tables 2 and 3 print only the two
  variances. Neither the article nor its supplement gives the covariance or the
  correlation, so both models carry a diagonal IIV (covariance 0). Exposure
  metrics that depend only on CL/F (steady-state AUC24, the paper's primary
  output) are unaffected; the individual elimination rate, and therefore the
  individual ka and peak-trough swing, are more variable than in the authors'
  model, most noticeably for glecaprevir with its very large variances.
- **ka tied to the individual elimination rate.** The paper estimates ka as a
  factor times ke = CL/V2 "to avoid flip-flop behavior" (Tables 2 and 3,
  footnote b). The model applies the factor to each patient's own CL/V2,
  including random effects and weight scaling, because only that form keeps
  every patient's ka above ke. The derived typical ka values (18.6 and
  10.1 1/day) are reproduced above.
- **Residual error as a variance.** The residual tables are headed "sigma^2"
  and the IIV variances round-trip exactly to the printed %CVs through
  sqrt(exp(omega) - 1), so 0.568 (GLE) and 0.229 (PIB) are taken as variances
  of a proportional error: SDs 0.754 and 0.479.
- **Formulation indicator.** The fixed F1 ratios (0.8 GLE, 1.2 PIB) apply to all
  Part 2 dosing. The intensive-PK children took separate GLE and PIB coated
  granules and the others a single packet of co-packaged granules; the paper
  uses one F1 ratio for both, and so does `FORM_GRANULE`.
- **Time unit.** The paper reports CL/F and Q/F in L/day, ka in 1/day and ALAG1
  in days; the model keeps day as the time unit. The vignette converts to hours
  for AUC24 in ng*h/mL.
- **Virtual DORA cohort weights.** Weights are truncated-normal draws from the
  ESM Table S1 mean, SD and range of each cohort, not the observed weights. The
  paper's Table 4 values are geometric means of post hoc individual estimates
  in the patients who received the final dose (n = 17-44 per cohort), so a
  population simulation is not expected to match row by row.
- **Simulated AUC24.** The paper integrated its simulated last-day profiles with
  the linear trapezoidal rule on the intensive-PK sampling times (Table 1:
  0, 2, 4, 6 and 12 h after the dose); this vignette integrates a 0.5 h grid. Each weight band holds 200
  virtual children instead of a share of 10,000. With the diagonal IIV a few
  glecaprevir patients have half-lives of minutes and a grid AUC near zero;
  medians rather than geometric means are therefore compared, and the
  seed-free closed-form check confirms the geometric means.
- **Pibrentasvir is not at steady state on day 14.** The slow peripheral phase
  leaves the typical day-14 AUC24 3-8% below F x Dose / CL. The paper's
  simulation design (14 days of dosing) is kept for the comparison with its
  results.
- **No erratum.** No correction notice for the article was found as of
  2026-11-14.
